# shelby-viz: Dashboard Engine for Shelby Pipelines

shelby-viz is a Python/Jinja2 dashboard renderer that pulls live data from a running Shelby Go server and displays it as an auto-refreshing HTML grid of widgets. It has no database—it reads directly from the Shelby HTTP API at render time.

## Installation & CLI

```bash
pip install -e .          # from this directory
# or: pip install shelby-viz

shelby-viz serve  <dashboard-dir> [--shelby http://localhost:8080] [--port 5000] [--debug]
shelby-viz build  <dashboard-dir> [--shelby http://localhost:8080] [--out dist/]
shelby-viz init   <name>          [--out .]
shelby-viz validate <dashboard-dir>
```

## Dashboard project layout

```
my-dashboard/
  dashboard.yml          ← required: widget grid definition
  widgets/               ← optional: custom Jinja2 templates (.html.j2)
  assets/                ← optional: CSS/JS referenced by custom widgets
  vars/                  ← optional: environment-specific variable overrides
```

## dashboard.yml — full reference

```yaml
name: My Dashboard          # required
description: Optional text  # optional
refresh: 30s                # polling interval — Ns | Nm | Nh  (default: 60s)

layout:
  columns: 12               # CSS grid column count (default: 12)

vars:                       # available in templates as {{ vars.key }}
  shelby_url: http://localhost:8080
  my_threshold: 90

widgets:
  - id: cpu                 # unique string within the dashboard
    title: CPU Usage        # displayed in widget header
    type: gauge             # gauge | timeseries | counter | table | status | custom
    col: 1                  # grid column start (1-based)
    row: 1                  # grid row start (1-based)
    width: 4                # columns to span
    height: 2               # rows to span

    binding:                # keys here become data.<key> inside the template
      value:                # ← binding key name (any string you choose)
        pipeline: my-slug   # Shelby pipeline slug
        series: cpu.percent # dotted field path in the pipeline output
        limit: 2            # last N runs (default: 50)
        unit: "%"           # optional unit hint forwarded to the API

    config:                 # free-form dict forwarded verbatim as config.* in templates
      min: 0
      max: 100
      unit: "%"
```

## Binding shapes

All bindings live under the `binding:` key. Each binding key (`value:`, `series:`, `rows:`, `status:`, etc.) can use one of four shapes:

### 1. Series binding (most common)
```yaml
binding:
  value:
    pipeline: my-pipeline
    series: some.field
    limit: 50      # optional, default 50
    unit: ms       # optional
```
Returns a `SeriesData` object. Access via `data.value.*` in templates.

### 2. Runs binding
```yaml
binding:
  runs:
    pipeline: my-pipeline
    runs: 20       # limit
```
Returns the raw JSON dict from `/api/pipelines/:slug/runs`.

### 3. Static binding
```yaml
binding:
  threshold:
    value: 42
```
Returns the literal value.

### 4. Expression binding (advanced)
```yaml
binding:
  computed: "{{ pipelines['my-slug'].series('field.path') }}"
```
The string is evaluated as a Python expression with `pipelines` in scope.

## SeriesData API (available in widget templates as `data.<key>`)

```
data.key            → SeriesData object
data.key.last       → float  — most recent value
data.key.previous   → float  — second-most-recent value
data.key.trend      → float  — last - previous
data.key.max        → float
data.key.min        → float
data.key.avg        → float
data.key.points     → list of {t: str, v: float, run_id: str}
data.key.unit       → str
data.key.kind       → str  ("timeseries")
len(data.key)       → int  — number of points
bool(data.key)      → False when empty
```

## Built-in widget types

| type | required binding key | required config | notes |
|------|---------------------|-----------------|-------|
| `gauge` | `value` (SeriesData) | `min`, `max`, `unit` | semicircle arc, color shifts green→red |
| `timeseries` | `series` (SeriesData) | `unit`, `color` (opt) | bar chart, shows avg/max in footer |
| `counter` | `value` (SeriesData) | `unit` | large number + trend arrow |
| `table` | `rows` (SeriesData) | `unit` (opt) | scrollable table of last 20 points |
| `status` | `status` (SeriesData) | `ok_above` or `error_above` (opt) | colored dot — ok / warning / error |

### gauge config options
```yaml
config:
  min: 0
  max: 100
  unit: "%"
  error_above: 85    # optional — value >= this renders red
```

### status config options
```yaml
config:
  ok_above: 0.1      # value >= threshold → ok, else warning
  # OR
  error_above: 85    # value >= threshold → error, else ok
  # (if neither is set: truthy value → ok, falsy → error)
```

## Custom widgets

Set `type: custom` and provide a `template:` path (relative to the dashboard project root):

```yaml
- id: my-widget
  type: custom
  template: widgets/my-widget.html.j2
  col: 1
  row: 1
  width: 6
  height: 3
  binding:
    used:
      pipeline: my-pipeline
      series: memory.used
      limit: 2
    total:
      pipeline: my-pipeline
      series: memory.total
      limit: 2
  config:
    show_trend: true
```

Inside the template, three variables are available:

```jinja2
{{ data }}        {# dict of resolved bindings — data.used, data.total, etc. #}
{{ config }}      {# free-form dict from dashboard.yml config: block #}
{{ meta.title }}  {# widget title string #}
{{ meta.id }}     {# widget id string #}
```

Widgets render inside Shadow DOM cells — your CSS is fully isolated.

### Custom widget skeleton
```jinja2
{%- set val = data.mykey.last | default(0) | float -%}
<style>
  :host { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 100%; }
  .value { font-size: 2rem; font-weight: 700; color: #e0e0ff; }
</style>
<div class="value">{{ val | round(1) }} {{ config.unit | default('') }}</div>
```

## Jinja2 filters added by shelby-viz

| filter | signature | example |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| `filesizeformat` | `(value, binary=False)` | `{{ bytes \| filesizeformat }}` → `"1.4 GB"` |
| `ratio` | `(value, total)` | `{{ used \| ratio(total) }}` → `0.73` |
| `abs` | `(value)` | `{{ trend \| abs }}` |

Standard Jinja2 filters (`round`, `default`, `float`, `int`, `min`, `max`, `list`, `reverse`, etc.) are also available.

## Architecture

```
Shelby Go binary  →  HTTP API
  GET /api/pipelines/:slug/series?field=&limit=&unit=
  GET /api/pipelines/:slug/runs?limit=
         │
         ▼
shelby-viz (Python)
  loader.py   — parses dashboard.yml → DashboardDef / WidgetDef dataclasses
  data.py     — PipelinesContext, PipelineProxy, SeriesData
  renderer.py — resolves bindings + renders .html.j2 via Jinja2
  server.py   — Flask dev server with /api/widget/:id polling endpoint
  cli.py      — Click CLI (serve / build / init / validate)
         │
         ▼
Browser
  CSS Grid host  (base.html shell)
  Shadow DOM per widget cell
  runtime.js  — polls /api/widget/:id every <refresh>s, swaps shadow root
```

## Worked example: system-health dashboard

This example connects to a `system-health` Shelby pipeline that emits `cpu.percent`, `memory.used`, `memory.total`, and `disk.percentage_used`.

```yaml
name: System Health
description: CPU, memory, disk and host metrics
refresh: 10s

layout:
  columns: 12

vars:
  shelby_url: http://localhost:8080

widgets:
  - id: cpu-gauge
    title: CPU Usage
    type: gauge
    col: 1
    row: 1
    width: 3
    height: 3
    binding:
      value:
        pipeline: system-health
        series: cpu.percent
        limit: 2
    config:
      min: 0
      max: 100
      unit: "%"

  - id: cpu-history
    title: CPU History
    type: timeseries
    col: 4
    row: 1
    width: 9
    height: 3
    binding:
      series:
        pipeline: system-health
        series: cpu.percent
        limit: 60
    config:
      unit: "%"
      color: "#00d4aa"

  - id: mem-donut
    title: Memory Breakdown
    type: custom
    template: widgets/memory-donut.html.j2
    col: 4
    row: 4
    width: 4
    height: 3
    binding:
      used:
        pipeline: system-health
        series: memory.used
        limit: 2
      total:
        pipeline: system-health
        series: memory.total
        limit: 2

  - id: pipeline-ok
    title: Pipeline Status
    type: status
    col: 11
    row: 4
    width: 2
    height: 3
    binding:
      status:
        pipeline: system-health
        series: cpu.percent
        limit: 1
    config:
      ok_above: 0.1

  - id: run-log
    title: Recent CPU Readings
    type: table
    col: 1
    row: 7
    width: 12
    height: 3
    binding:
      rows:
        pipeline: system-health
        series: cpu.percent
        limit: 20
```

## Common patterns

**Show bytes as human-readable size:**
```jinja2
{%- set bytes = data.used.last | default(0) | float -%}
{{ bytes | filesizeformat(binary=True) }}
```

**Threshold-based color:**
```jinja2
{%- set val = data.value.last | float -%}
{%- set color = '#4caf50' if val < 60 else ('#ff9800' if val < 85 else '#f44336') -%}
```

**Trend arrow:**
```jinja2
{%- set trend = data.value.trend | float -%}
{% if trend > 0 %}↑{% elif trend < 0 %}↓{% else %}→{% endif %}
{{ trend | abs | round(2) }}
```

**Iterate over all data points:**
```jinja2
{% for p in data.series.points %}
  <div>{{ p.t }} — {{ p.v | round(2) }}</div>
{% endfor %}
```

**Multiple bindings in one widget:**
```yaml
binding:
  used:
    pipeline: my-pipeline
    series: memory.used
    limit: 2
  total:
    pipeline: my-pipeline
    series: memory.total
    limit: 2
```
```jinja2
{%- set pct = (data.used.last / data.total.last * 100) | round(0) | int -%}
```

## Validation

```bash
shelby-viz validate my-dashboard/
# ✓ dashboard.yml — 6 widget(s)
# ✓ cpu-gauge (gauge) → widgets/gauge.html.j2
# ✓ mem-donut (custom) → widgets/memory-donut.html.j2
```

Validation checks: YAML parses, all referenced templates exist. It does not require a live Shelby server.

## Grid positioning rules

- The grid has `layout.columns` columns (default 12).
- `col` is 1-based; `col + width - 1` must be ≤ `columns`.
- `row` is 1-based; rows expand automatically — no declared row limit.
- Widgets can overlap if you intend layering; shelby-viz does not enforce non-overlap.

## Mobile / responsive behaviour

No extra configuration is required. Below 768 px the renderer automatically:
- Collapses the grid to a single full-width column.
- Stacks widgets in DOM order (row-first, top-to-bottom as declared in `dashboard.yml`).
- Sets a `min-height: 140px` per cell so short widgets don't collapse.

The positioning is implemented with CSS custom properties (`--sc`, `--sw`, `--sr`, `--sh`) so the `@media` block can override layout without fighting inline styles.

If the stacking order on mobile is wrong, reorder the `widgets:` list in `dashboard.yml` — desktop layout is driven by `col`/`row`, mobile order is DOM order.

## Dataclass reference (Python)

```python
@dataclass
class WidgetDef:
    id: str
    title: str
    type: str           # gauge | timeseries | counter | table | status | custom
    col: int
    row: int
    width: int
    height: int
    binding: dict       # raw binding config from YAML
    config: dict        # raw config from YAML
    template: str|None  # required when type == "custom"

@dataclass
class DashboardDef:
    name: str
    description: str
    refresh: int        # seconds (after parsing Ns/Nm/Nh)
    columns: int
    widgets: list[WidgetDef]
    vars: dict
```
